cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Detox – the process of abstaining from or ridding the body of toxic substances or unhealthy habits, especially digital devices.

p.em: Example: A digital detox is essential to recalibrate our chemical reward system and lower our anxiety levels.

cosy-blockquote.p: Boundary – a limit or dividing line that defines where one space, activity, or relationship ends and another begins.

p.em: Example: Establishing a strict bedroom boundary ensures that our sleep cycle remains completely protected from screens.

cosy-blockquote.p: Triage – the process of sorting and prioritizing tasks, applications, or problems based on their urgency or value.

p.em: Example: We must perform technology triage, deleting every application that steals our time without improving our life.

cosy-blockquote.p: Habitual ≠ deliberate – done constantly or repeatedly as a matter of common practice and subconscious habit ≠ done with active intention and care.

p.em: Example: Checking our screen is often habitual rather than deliberate, meaning we do it without any clear purpose in mind.

cosy-blockquote.p: To reclaim – to retrieve, recover, or win back something valuable that was previously lost or taken away.

p.em: Example: By putting away our devices during dinners, we can reclaim precious moments of genuine human connection.

cosy-blockquote.p: Solitary – done or experienced completely alone, without the presence or participation of other people.

p.em: Example: Engaging in a solitary walk allows our minds to relax and process daily events without virtual noise.

cosy-blockquote.p: Offline ≠ connected – not actively utilizing or connected to a digital network or the global internet ≠ permanently online or receiving data.

p.em: Example: We need more offline activities to balance our highly connected, screen-dominated work schedules.

cosy-blockquote.p: To nourish – to provide with the substance, energy, or support necessary for growth, physical health, and general life.

p.em: Example: We must find analog hobbies that nourish our creative spirit instead of consuming our time passively.

cosy-blockquote.p: To implement – to put a decision, plan, or process into active effect or physical operation.

p.em: Example: It is incredibly easy to read about detox plans, but highly challenging to implement them in our daily routine.

cosy-blockquote.p: To succeed ≠ fail – to achieve the desired aim, result, or positive outcome of an endeavor ≠ to fall short of success or be unsuccessful.

p.em: Example: If we set clear, realistic boundaries, we will succeed in building a healthy digital relationship, whereas ignoring rules causes us to fail.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What are the psychological benefits of executing a complete digital detox over a simple weekend break?
★ What is the longest period you spent entirely offline during the past twelve months?

How does establishing firm physical boundaries in our homes improve our sleeping habits?
★ Do you charge your phone on your nightstand, or do you leave it in another room?

Why is application triage a necessary first step when trying to reframe our digital routines?
★ Which application did you delete recently because it was wasting your time?

How can we distinguish between habitual screen checking and deliberate communication?
★ How many times a day do you think you click the lock screen without looking for anything specific?

What is the most effective way to reclaim our attention span after years of heavy screen reliance?
★ Which offline skill or project would you like to explore with your recovered free time?

Why do many people find peaceful, solitary thinking spaces incredibly uncomfortable to experience?
★ Do you prefer to think in silence while walking, or do you always wear headphones?

How do offline habits nourish our creative capacity in ways that digital feeds cannot replicate?
★ What physical, analog activity brings you the greatest sense of calm and accomplishment?

What are the primary logistical barriers when trying to implement a strict boundaries plan?
★ Do you think your professional colleagues would understand if you turned off your phone after hours?

Why do most people fail to succeed when attempting a sudden, extreme cold-turkey digital breakup?
★ Have you ever failed to maintain a healthy habit because the rules were too strict?

How does the permanent availability of digital inputs weaken our ability to manage natural real-world boredom?
★ What did you do to entertain yourself during long, boring car rides before you had a screen?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Future smart apartments will feature built-in Faraday shields to automatically enforce offline bedrooms. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you pay a higher rent to live in an apartment that blocks all wireless signals?

The corporate landscape will eventually enforce a weekly detox day where all business communications are completely banned. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you believe your company would be more productive if no one worked on Fridays?

Future parents will be legally prosecuted if they fail to implement strict device limits for their children. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think government laws are necessary to protect minors from screen addiction?

Analog hobbies like pottery, gardening, and carpentry will completely replace digital coding as core career paths of the future. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could earn the same salary, would you prefer a manual job over a computer desk job?

Smartphones will soon become entirely obsolete, replaced by intelligent glasses that show data only when we focus our eyes. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you wear smart glasses if they completely freed your hands from holding a device?

In the future, a person's social status will be determined by their capacity to experience absolute, peaceful solitude. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you view people who are completely absent from social media as mysterious or outdated?

Tech developers will design artificial minds that nourish our biological brains by simulating the effects of real-world forests. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you wear virtual reality glasses to relax in a digital forest during lunch break?

The successful citizens of tomorrow will be those who refuse to establish any habitual, permanent connection to the global internet. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you believe it is possible to maintain a highly successful career while staying completely offline?

Future applications will use biometric feedback to automatically lock themselves when they detect a user is feeling habitual fatigue. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you install an app that blocks you from social media when it detects you are tired?

To protect baseline cognitive skills, future schools will teach children how to write elegantly with ink pens as a core exam subject. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think typing is reducing your capability to formulate complex arguments on paper?

ul.li: Incorrect: It is crucial that he implements the boundaries plan. → Correct: It is crucial that he implement the boundaries plan. ((Underlined subjunctive verb. After 'it is crucial/essential/important that...', use the base verb form 'implement' without third-person 's'))

Incorrect: We had better to delete the addictive applications. → Correct: We had better delete the addictive applications. ((The modal structure 'had better' is followed directly by the bare infinitive verb, not the infinitive with 'to'))

Incorrect: If we set limits, we will success in our detox. → Correct: If we set limits, we will succeed in our detox. ((Underlined vocabulary choice: 'success' is a noun, whereas the verb form is 'succeed'))
